chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Adapting gags for English audiences
summary: American jokes like the window-shades gag did not land, so they changed the material and kept other bits.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Mr. Bubbles, you've talked to me before about how you were able to feel an audience out and you had a natural ability to sell your performance to an audience and you were just mentioning about the English audience that you had to feel them out. How were they different and did you change your act? Did you do anything different for them?
No, they're the same, but we had to change it around to make it meet with their sense of viewing. Because what was humorous to America wasn't humorous to English.
Can you give me an example?

For instance, the gag I used to pull, 'I passed by your house last night. I seen you kissing your wife. Why didn't you pull your window shades down? Ha-ha-ha. What you're laughing about, I wasn't even home last night.' That humor is different in

England. You would say it in a different way. I'm still trying to learn it -- so I didn't learn it, so you better leave and come back to America. Because the gags ain't going over like this, you know. But we were successful otherwise, all other bits we'd do, like get out of that hole, you little old man -- that was going over all right. "What's that I see walking down your neck?" "That's a mole, man" -- No, "What's that on your neck?" "That's a mole," He's walking." "If you had $5.00 in your pocket, what would you thing?" "I think I had on somebody else's pants." And "Who's that lady I saw you with on the Freeway last night." "That was no lady, that was my wife." These were all different for England, you know.
That was all different humor, you know. Things don't go as good over there as they do over here in that category. So you had to change it around. And

what you change it to, you'll find out, you can't wait forever to find out you have to come back directly to find out, it seemed like. 'Cause by the time you try to get the gags to fit the personalities, you could starve to death.
